checks.s: The memo contains a clearly labeled Section 1, Executive Summary.
The memo contains a clearly labeled Section 2, Transaction Overview.
The memo contains a clearly labeled Section 3, Authority Analysis.
The memo contains a clearly labeled Section 4, Out-of-Policy Terms.
The memo contains a clearly labeled Section 5, Risk Assessment.
The memo contains a clearly labeled Section 6, Recommended Compromise Positions.
The memo contains a clearly labeled Section 7, Timeline and Deadline.
The memo contains a clearly labeled Section 8, Recommendation and Approval Request.
The memo contains a clearly labeled Section 9, Signature/Approval blocks.

The nine sections appear in this order: (1) Executive Summary, (2) Transaction Overview, (3) Authority Analysis, (4) Out-of-Policy Terms, (5) Risk Assessment, (6) Recommended Compromise Positions, (7) Timeline and Deadline, (8) Recommendation and Approval Request, (9) Signature blocks.
The memo is addressed to both Dr. Lena Marchetti (CLO, Tier 4 approver) and Raymond Achebe (VP Business Development, Tier 3 approver).
The memo shows it is from Nadia Kowalski, Senior Contracts Manager.
The memo’s CC line includes Col. (Ret.) Derek Saldaña (SVP, Capture Management) and Sean Nakamura (Halyard & Calloway LLP, outside counsel).
The Transaction Overview identifies VDS as prospective prime contractor and CIS as prospective major subcontractor for the GaN-based RF amplifier subsystem.
The memo states the solicitation number FA8812-25-R-0049.
The memo identifies the program codename as STORMLIGHT.
The memo states the estimated total contract value (TCV) is $187,000,000 (or $187M).
The memo states the period of performance is 8 years total, consisting of a 5-year base period plus a 3-year option period.
The memo states CIS’s proposed workshare is 34% of TCV, equaling $63,580,000 (or $63.58M).
The memo states or derives CIS annual contract value (ACV) as $7,947,500 (or approximately $7.9475M).
The Authority Analysis states that the CIS subcontract value of $63,580,000 falls within Tier 3 on value alone, under the Tier 3 threshold of ≤$75M TCV.

The Authority Analysis identifies Exclusivity Scope (Annex B Item 4) and IP License-Back (Annex B Item 1) as two of the five CRP Annex B Red Line items requiring mandatory Tier 4 / CLO approval regardless of contract value.

The Authority Analysis identifies Workshare Guarantee/MFT (Annex A Item 9), Liability Cap (Annex A Item 12), and Break-Up Fee (Annex A Item 15) as the three Tier 3 deviations requiring VP BD approval.
The memo states CIS demands mutual exclusivity across all DoD EW programs for 36 months.
The memo states the VDS pre-approved fallback is exclusivity limited to the STORMLIGHT solicitation only, expiring upon award or 12 months, whichever is earlier.
The memo states the exclusivity delta is 24 additional months of duration and an expansion of scope to all DoD EW programs beyond STORMLIGHT only.
The memo quantifies the pipeline risk as the $412,000,000 combined value of VDS’s three other active EW captures at risk from broad exclusivity.
The memo classifies Term 1 as a Red Line item per CRP Annex B Item 4.
The memo states CIS demands a guaranteed minimum 30% workshare ($56,100,000 floor) plus an automatic +5 percentage point ratchet if any other teammate exceeds 15% workshare.
The memo states the MFT ratchet could push CIS workshare to a potential ceiling of 39% / $72,930,000.
The memo states the VDS approved fallback is a best-efforts workshare target of 25–35% with no MFT clause.
The memo quantifies the MFT ratchet exposure delta at $16,830,000 ($72,930,000 – $56,100,000).
The memo classifies Term 2 as a Tier 3 deviation per CRP Annex A Item 9 (Workshare Guarantees/MFT).
The memo states CIS demands an irrevocable, royalty-free, worldwide license to all VDS background IP incorporated into the joint solution for any purpose, including commercial resale.
The memo states the VDS approved fallback is a limited, revocable, contract-scope-only license with no commercial-use rights.
The memo quantifies the VDS EW background IP portfolio at risk at $28,000,000 (per VDS Technology Office valuation).
The memo flags potential conflicts with existing VDS IP licensing agreements or third-party obligations.
The memo classifies Term 3 as a Red Line item per CRP Annex B Item 1 (Background IP License-Back).
The memo states CIS demands a $2,000,000 aggregate liability cap excluding only willful misconduct.
The memo states the VDS approved fallback is a liability cap of 100% of fees paid in the trailing 12-month period, equaling $7,947,500.
The memo states the CIS cap of $2M is only 25.16% of the VDS policy minimum ($7,947,500).
The memo states the shortfall between the VDS policy minimum and CIS cap is $5,947,500.
The memo references Ridgeline Risk Advisors’ analysis identifying an uncovered insurance gap of approximately $5,900,000 per occurrence.
The memo references Ridgeline’s recommendation to either negotiate the cap to at least $4,000,000 or purchase supplemental coverage at $185,000–$220,000 per annum.
The memo classifies Term 4 as a Tier 3 deviation per CRP Annex A Item 12 (Limitation of Liability).
The memo states CIS demands a $4,500,000 break-up fee payable if VDS terminates for convenience or re-teams prior to award.
The memo states the VDS approved fallback is no break-up fee, with each party bearing its own B&P costs.
The memo notes that outside counsel found VDS has no precedent for break-up fees exceeding $1,000,000 in teaming agreements.
The memo classifies Term 5 as a Tier 3 deviation per CRP Annex A Item 15 (Termination/Break-Up Fees).
The memo recommends a Term 1 compromise of mutual exclusivity limited to STORMLIGHT plus any directly competing EW solicitation, with an 18-month term.
The memo characterizes the residual risk for the Term 1 compromise as moderate and notes that 2 of 3 other pipeline captures would be excluded from the exclusivity scope.
The memo recommends a Term 2 compromise of a 28% hard floor ($52,360,000), no MFT ratchet, and a soft target of 34%.
The memo characterizes the residual risk for the Term 2 compromise as low-to-moderate (or low to moderate).

The memo recommends a Term 3 compromise of a non-exclusive, limited license for CIS to use VDS background IP in CIS’s performance of the STORMLIGHT subcontract plus any direct follow-on, revocable 24 months after program end, with no commercial resale rights.
The memo characterizes the residual risk for the Term 3 compromise as low.
The memo recommends a Term 4 compromise of a liability cap at 50% of trailing 12-month fees ($3,973,750), with carve-outs for IP infringement and bodily injury.
The memo characterizes the residual risk for the Term 4 compromise as moderate, noting it is still below policy minimum but approximately doubles CIS’s original ask.

The memo recommends a Term 5 compromise of a $1,500,000 break-up fee payable only if VDS re-teams with a CIS-identified competitor within 6 months of TA execution, with no fee for simple convenience termination.
The memo characterizes the residual risk for the Term 5 compromise as low, noting the $3,000,000 reduction from CIS’s ask and the narrowly scoped trigger.
The memo states Tier 2 fallback positions were exhausted on 25 June 2025.
The memo states the internal TA execution deadline is 18 July 2025.
The memo states the proposal due date is 15 August 2025.
The memo explains that the 28-calendar-day rule from Capture Process Guide §6.3 requires TA execution 28 days before the proposal due date, driving the 18 July deadline.
The memo requests approval by 11 July 2025.
The memo states CIS is the sole domestic manufacturer (or sole qualified source) of the GaN-based RF amplifier subsystem critical to the STORMLIGHT technical solution.
The memo states no viable alternative teammates have been identified.
The memo states VDS Pwin drops from 65% to below 20% without CIS.
The memo states STORMLIGHT is VDS’s highest-priority EW capture for FY25–FY26, or uses equivalent wording conveying top priority.
The memo includes a signature/approval block for Dr. Lena Marchetti identifying her as CLO and Tier 4 approver for the two Red Line terms.
The memo includes a signature/approval block for Raymond Achebe identifying him as VP Business Development and Tier 3 approver for the three non-Red-Line terms.

For each of the five terms, the Risk Assessment section provides at least one risk category (financial, legal, strategic, operational, or reputational), likelihood, impact, and an overall risk rating.
The memo states the VDS initial draft was sent 19 May 2025 and the CIS redline was received 2 June 2025.
The memo documents three negotiation sessions held on 9 June, 17 June, and 25 June 2025.
The memo states VDS offered Tier 1 alternatives at Session 2 (17 June), exercised all Tier 2 fallback positions at Session 3 (25 June), and CIS declined to move on all five terms.

The memo affirmatively states Board notice is NOT required because the relevant subcontract value ($63,580,000 base, up to $72,930,000 with MFT ratchet) is below the $100,000,000 TCV threshold for Board notice under Tier 4.
The memo references as supporting legal analysis the outside counsel risk assessment from Halyard & Calloway LLP by Sean Nakamura, engagement HC-VDS-2025-0187, dated 28 June 2025.
The memo or the outside counsel risk assessment is marked privileged and confidential.

The Term 4 (Liability Cap) risk assessment references the Ridgeline Risk Advisors insurance analysis and states both the approximately $5,900,000 uncovered insurance gap per occurrence and the $185,000–$220,000 per annum supplemental coverage cost estimate.

The memo notes that per Capture Process Guide §6.5, SVP-level waiver authority permits an extension of up to 7 calendar days if the 18 July deadline cannot be met, providing a backstop through 25 July 2025.

The Executive Summary concisely frames the risk of five out-of-policy terms with financial, legal, and/or strategic risk and the strategic imperative that losing CIS reduces Pwin from 65% to below 20% on a $187M program that is VDS’s top EW capture priority, warranting executive consideration of compromise positions.
The memo identifies VDS as a Delaware LLC with CAGE code 7VD42 and DUNS number 08-441-9327.
The memo identifies CIS as a Virginia corporation with CAGE code 3CS88 and DUNS number 62-710-5583.
